name: Eliakim
bio:
Eliakim son of Hilkiah was in charge of Hezekiah's household. Along with Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder, he went out to meet Sennacherib's officers Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh when they came against Jerusalem, and heard Rabshakeh's mocking speech threatening the city and urging surrender. Eliakim asked Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic rather than Hebrew so the people on the wall wouldn't understand, but Rabshakeh refused and shouted his threats in Hebrew anyway. Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah returned to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, reporting Rabshakeh's words (2 Kings 18:18-37).

## 📖 Core Story: Sent to Isaiah

After Rabshakeh's threats, Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests — all in sackcloth — to the prophet Isaiah to ask him to pray for the besieged city. Isaiah's reassuring answer, and the LORD's destruction of Sennacherib's army that followed, are described in Hezekiah's own story (2 Kings 19:1-7).
